title: Email suite security and administrator settings
source_system: Email and file suite admin console (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Business plan with one user, the owner, whose daily account is also the suite administrator; password sign-in, with MFA (authenticator app or security key) available and turned off; account recovery by text message to the phone; the provider keeps a sign-in history and a log of settings changes; spam and phishing filtering on; no third-party backup connected; deleted items can be recovered only within the provider's retention period

title: Mailbox and file storage content review
source_system: Email and file suite (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Folders hold pickup authorizations, BOL PDFs, the order and shipment workbook, the SDS library, customer end-use statements, carrier emails with driver names and license numbers going back to 2022, the PHMSA registration certificates, and the 2022 training certificate; the laptop disk encryption recovery key is saved in a file; no retention or deletion rule is set on any folder; no copy of these files was found outside the suite

title: Accounting SaaS users, security settings and backup terms
source_system: Accounting SaaS admin settings (SYS-02); vendor service terms
what_it_shows: Two users: the owner (administrator) and the outside accountant's own user; the vendor enforces MFA for every user; the vendor's service terms state that it backs up customer data; invoices, receivables, payables, and customer and supplier bank details are held here

title: Bank portal user, sign-in and payee settings
source_system: Business bank online portal (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: One user (the owner); sign-in codes are sent by text message to the phone; new payees can be added online by that user; payee-change alerts are available and turned off; suppliers are paid by wire or ACH from this portal

title: Browser saved sign-ins and partner portal accounts
source_system: Laptop browser password store (SYS-05; SYS-04)
what_it_shows: Saved sign-ins for 9 supplier, carrier and ERI provider portal accounts and for the email suite; the browser's password check flags the email password as also used for one carrier portal; no separate password manager is installed

title: Laptop settings review
source_system: Laptop settings screens (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: One user account, the owner's, which is an administrator and is used for daily work; the owner states that family members sometimes use the laptop under this account; built-in disk encryption on since purchase in 2024; built-in antivirus on with real-time protection; automatic OS and browser updates on; host firewall on

title: Phone settings and phone carrier account
source_system: Mobile phone settings screens (SYS-06); phone carrier account portal
what_it_shows: Passcode and device encryption on; find-my-device on; automatic updates on; the email app, calls and texts with dispatchers and drivers, and the bank and email sign-in codes are on this phone; the camera roll holds photos of signed BOLs texted by drivers; the carrier account shows no port-out or SIM-change PIN set

title: Home office and home network walk-through
source_system: Home office (observation); ISP router label and network settings (SYS-07)
what_it_shows: Home office in the owner's residence with no chemicals on site; paper is kept in a locked desk drawer and a cross-cut shredder is used for paper; the ISP-provided router has its admin credentials printed on its label, and the owner states the admin password was never changed; household devices and the business laptop share one Wi-Fi network

title: Search of the owner's files for security and hazmat security documents
source_system: Laptop; email and file suite; paper files
what_it_shows: No written hazmat transportation security plan, transportation security risk assessment, information security policy, incident plan or contact list, vendor list, record of a review of any SaaS vendor's security report, retention or disposal rule, coverage arrangement, or rule for checking AI-drafted text was found

title: PHMSA hazmat registration certificate and registration history
source_system: PHMSA registration portal; email folder (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Certificate of Registration for the registration year 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30, under 107.601(a)(4) (bulk packaging of 3,500 gallons or more) and (a)(6) (placarded quantities); the portal lists a registration for each year since 2022

title: HMR training record and course outline
source_system: Hazmat training provider account; email folder (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: One completed online HMR course with test, 2022-06, covering general awareness, function-specific training (shipping papers and emergency response information), safety, and security awareness; the security awareness module is a general overview; no later course or certificate appears in the account; no in-depth security training course was taken

title: ERI provider service contract and BOL template
source_system: Signed agreements folder; BOL template (SYS-01 files); ERI provider portal (SYS-04)
what_it_shows: 24-hour emergency response information service under a current contract; the BOL template prints the provider's telephone number and the company's contract number; the most recent product list confirmation from the provider in the inbox is dated 2024

title: Order and shipment workbook, 12 months to 2026-08-31
source_system: Order and shipment workbook (SYS-01 files)
what_it_shows: About 40 active business customers with Florida and south Georgia ship-to addresses and about 75 orders a year; every order is drop-shipped from one of 5 suppliers' plants or terminals by one of about 6 for-hire carriers; products: hydrogen peroxide 50% (about 6 cargo tank loads of about 4,000 gallons to 2 customers and about 20 totes), sodium hypochlorite, sodium hydroxide, ferric chloride (first sold in 2025), and polymers and defoamers; no hydrochloric acid, sulfuric acid or potassium permanganate; no export orders

title: Customer end-use statements
source_system: Email and file suite (SYS-01 files)
what_it_shows: An end-use statement is on file for each hydrogen peroxide customer in the order workbook

title: Supplier distribution agreements and product stewardship terms
source_system: Signed agreements folder
what_it_shows: Agreements with the 5 suppliers; the supplier fills, marks, labels, placards and loads, and releases each load against the owner's pickup authorization, and its shipping clerk checks the driver at the dock; the hydrogen peroxide producers' product stewardship terms require an end-use statement from each customer and a yearly distributor review, which in 2026 asks how the distributor prevents fraudulent orders and pickups

title: Inbox sample: pickup authorizations, carrier bookings and change requests, 2026
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Each pickup authorization email gives the supplier the carrier, driver name, truck number and a pickup number; carrier rate confirmations and tracking links arrive by email, and carriers email driver names with license numbers, which the owner forwards to the supplier's shipping clerk; ship-to changes, carrier and driver changes, and supplier bank-detail notices arrive by email and were answered by reply email; no note of a call-back appears in the emails or the workbook

title: The 2026-06-17 lookalike-domain order request
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: A message from a domain resembling an existing customer's domain asked for a hydrogen peroxide tote to be shipped to a new address for a second site; it was delivered to the inbox, not the junk folder; no order was entered in the workbook; no log entry or message to the customer, a supplier or law enforcement about it was found; the owner states the tote was not shipped because the customer's buyer called that day

title: The 2026-05 ferric chloride BOL correction
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: An email thread from 2026-05 in which a supplier's shipping clerk questioned Packing Group II on a ferric chloride BOL; the owner sent a corrected BOL showing Packing Group III before pickup; the owner states the first description was drafted with the AI assistant

title: Bank and card statements, 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31
source_system: Business bank account and card statements
what_it_shows: Recurring payments to the email and file suite provider, the accounting SaaS vendor, the ERI provider, the phone carrier, the ISP, the general and products liability insurer, and the generative AI assistant vendor (paid individual plan, monthly from 2026-03); payments to the CPA firm, the business attorney and the computer shop; wires and ACH payments to the 5 suppliers and payments to carriers; customer ACH receipts; no payment for a cyber insurance policy

title: Computer shop invoices
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Hourly invoices for laptop and router help on request; one 2025 invoice lists a remote-support session; no support contract or standing access

title: General and products liability policy declarations
source_system: Insurance agent portal
what_it_shows: General and products liability coverage in force; no cyber coverage is listed on the declarations page

title: 2025 Schedule C (Form 1040)
source_system: Owner's tax files (prepared by the CPA firm)
what_it_shows: Gross receipts of about $180,000; no wages paid; the business is a sole proprietorship with no employees

title: Email suite provider SOC 2 Type 2 report and bridge letter
source_system: Email suite provider trust portal
what_it_shows: Type 2 report on the Security, Availability and Confidentiality categories for the 12 months ending 2026-06-30, unqualified opinion, no test exceptions noted; lists complementary user entity controls (enable MFA, manage users and admin roles, review sign-in and audit logs, configure retention and backup of customer data, report suspected compromise); data center colocation providers are carved-out subservice organizations; bridge letter dated 2026-07-15

title: Generative AI assistant plan and data terms
source_system: AI assistant account page and vendor terms (SYS-08)
what_it_shows: Paid individual plan in the owner's name since 2026-03; password sign-in; the plan terms let the vendor use chats to improve its models unless the user turns that setting off; the vendor offers business plans whose terms exclude customer data from training

title: Invoice template and receivables report
source_system: Accounting SaaS (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: Invoices print the company's bank account number for ACH payment; about half of customers paid by ACH in the last 12 months

title: BIA self-review worksheet
source_system: Owner's written BIA worksheet, reviewed with the IT technician
what_it_shows: For each of the five business functions, the owner's account of the systems, partners and manual workaround used, and the longest outage and data loss the function can tolerate; one bulk hydrogen peroxide load is worth about $15,000; bulk loads are scheduled 3 to 5 days ahead; suppliers give 30-day terms; the owner is the only person who performs or authorizes each function

title: Risk walk-through of accounts and devices
source_system: Walk-through of every account, the laptop, the phone and the router with the IT technician
what_it_shows: The router admin page accepted the default credentials from the label and shows no firmware update status; the browser's password check still flags the email password as reused on one carrier portal; the laptop antivirus was on with real-time protection and same-day signatures; bank and accounting codes and email account recovery all go to the one phone; the two 2026 near misses (EV-017, EV-018) were walked through as threat events

title: Gap analysis self-review
source_system: Owner's written answers to the HMR, CFATS benchmark and Florida questions, checked on screen with the IT technician
what_it_shows: The owner determines the hazard class from the SDS, prepares the BOL and provides the emergency response information, and the supplier fills, marks, labels, placards and loads; this split had not been written down; the owner believed the suppliers' security plans covered the drop shipments; carriers are chosen on price and availability, with no check of a carrier's own security plan and no rule for a late or off-route load; the 2026-06-17 request was not reported to the customer, a supplier or law enforcement; there is no breach procedure or contact list, and the owner did not know Florida's law covered driver data

title: 2026 BOL sample compared with the Hazardous Materials Table
source_system: 10 BOLs from 2026 (SYS-01 files); 49 CFR 172.101 table
what_it_shows: Descriptions were typed or pasted per order from earlier BOLs, and descriptions for new products since 2026-03 were drafted with the AI assistant; each BOL was compared with the 172.101 table entry for its product; each carries the shipper's certification signed with a typed name and the ERI provider's number and contract number; each BOL package email attaches the product's SDS

title: Records and email folder review
source_system: Email and file suite (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Registration certificates for the current and 2025-2026 years are in the email folder, and the 2024-2025 registration statement copy was not found; BOL PDFs are kept in email and files; carrier-signed copies with the acceptance date came back for about half of loads; the 2022 training certificate is kept in email with no description or location of the training materials and no trainer address

title: ERI provider product list export and reconciliation
source_system: ERI provider portal (SYS-04); order and shipment workbook
what_it_shows: The provider's product list for the company covers hydrogen peroxide, sodium hypochlorite and sodium hydroxide and does not include ferric chloride; the order workbook shows four ferric chloride totes shipped since 2025

title: Mailbox search for driver records
source_system: Email and file suite (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: About 140 driver records (name with driver license number) in carrier emails from 2022 to 2026; most drivers live in Florida or Georgia; none has been deleted

title: Order workbook review for loads in transit
source_system: Order and shipment workbook (SYS-01 files)
what_it_shows: The workbook has no record of which loads are in transit and no delivery confirmation; shipments are released by email and tracking links arrive by email

title: Call with the hydrogen peroxide producer's distribution security contact and shipping office
source_system: Phone call notes
what_it_shows: The producer's security plan covers the producer's own functions (filling, loading and dock release), not the broker's order, shipping paper and pickup authorization functions; the producer's shipping clerk prints the BOL and the SDS for the driver at loading

title: ERI provider confirmation of the product list update
source_system: ERI provider email
what_it_shows: The provider confirmed in writing that ferric chloride was added to the company's product list

title: Regulatory status checks
source_system: eCFR (point-in-time 2026-09-23); Federal Register; Florida Legislature statutes site; vertical registry
what_it_shows: CFATS authority lapsed on 2023-07-28, and no reauthorization or CFATS document appears in the Federal Register in 2026 (vertical registry entry checked 2026-09-25); no CIRCIA final rule; no final rule on the HM-215R proposal (91 FR 5996); the eCFR text includes the PHMSA final rules of 2026-08-04

title: AI assistant data settings and chat history review
source_system: AI assistant account settings and chat history (SYS-08)
what_it_shows: The setting that lets the vendor use chats to improve its models was on, and the owner turned it off that day; the chat history since 2026-03 holds customer names, prices and SDS text, and no driver license numbers, pickup numbers, schedules or bank details; 7 hazmat descriptions were drafted in chats from 2026-03 to 2026-08

title: AI hazmat description accuracy check
source_system: AI assistant chats (SYS-08); 49 CFR 172.101 table
what_it_shows: Of the 7 descriptions drafted from 2026-03 to 2026-08, checked against the 172.101 table, 1 showed the wrong packing group (ferric chloride, PG II instead of III); in 5 new chats asking for the UN2014 description, 1 left out the subsidiary class 8

title: Control assessment: Laptop daily account test
source_system: Laptop account settings; software install attempt from the daily account
what_it_shows: The daily account is an administrator; a software install from it completed with no prompt for separate credentials; the owner states family members use the same account

title: Control assessment: Social engineering training self-review
source_system: 2022 course outline; 2026-06-17 lookalike-domain message; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The 2022 course outline has a general security awareness module and nothing on lookalike domains, fictitious pickups, social mining or payment fraud; no other training since; the 2026-06-17 message was not recognized as coming from a lookalike domain and was not reported

title: Control assessment: Role-based training review
source_system: Training certificate; course outline; training provider catalog; owner self-review
what_it_shows: Function-specific HMR training (shipping papers, emergency response information) was completed and tested in 2022-06 before the first shipment; no recurrent course since; no in-depth security training; no privacy training on driver data; no training when bulk loads or ferric chloride were added; the provider's 2026 catalog states its HMR course is updated each year for regulatory changes; the 2026 near misses do not appear in the owner's training notes

title: Control assessment: Sign-in, forwarding rule and payee review
source_system: Email sign-in history and forwarding rules; bank payee list; owner self-review
what_it_shows: No record of any review of email sign-ins, forwarding rules or bank payees; the forwarding rule scan found one rule sending copies of incoming mail to a former personal address, set up by the owner years ago and removed on 2026-09-10; no rule to act on review results or to increase review after a suspicious message

title: Control assessment: Backup review and restore test
source_system: Email suite SOC 2 report; accounting SaaS backup statement; suite retention settings; restore attempt
what_it_shows: Email, files, BOLs, the workbook, and the training and registration certificates have no backup outside the suite; a BOL deleted in 2025 could not be restored; the email suite SOC 2 report and the accounting SaaS backup statement describe provider backups that are encrypted, integrity-checked and kept in a separate region

title: Control assessment: Administrator MFA sign-in tests
source_system: Email suite and accounting SaaS security settings; sign-in tests from a new browser
what_it_shows: Accounting SaaS administrator sign-in required a second factor; the email suite administrator account, also the daily account, signed in with a password only

title: Control assessment: User account MFA sign-in tests
source_system: Email, bank and 9 partner portal sign-in tests from a new browser
what_it_shows: Bank sign-in required a text-message code; the email account and 7 of 9 partner portals signed in with a password only and offer no other factor; the other 2 portals offer MFA and it was turned off

title: Control assessment: Incident reporting self-review
source_system: Contact lists; supplier and ERI agreements; 2026-06-17 near miss; owner self-review
what_it_shows: No reporting time is defined and there is no list of whom to notify (producer, carrier, law enforcement, bank, drivers, Florida Department of Legal Affairs); the 2026-06-17 suspicious order was not logged or reported

title: Control assessment: Risk assessment review
source_system: P01 risk register; P05 BIA; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The 2026 risk assessment identifies 15 threat events, including the two 2026 near misses, rates likelihood and impact with SP 800-30 Tables G-5 and I-2, rates harm to drivers from exposure of license numbers, and is documented in the register and report; no review frequency or update trigger was defined at the time of assessment

title: Control assessment: Vendor review
source_system: Vendor terms; email suite SOC 2 report; ERI provider product list; AI assistant data terms; partner portal settings
what_it_shows: Every vendor except the ERI provider is on click-through terms; no security or privacy requirements are set for any vendor and no vendor list exists; the ERI product list did not include ferric chloride; the AI assistant's plan terms let the vendor use chats to improve its models unless the setting is turned off; 7 of 9 partner portals offer no MFA; the email suite SOC 2 report lists customer responsibilities and the ERI contract defines what the registrant must supply; only the email suite's assurance report was on file
